public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Zariski Cancellation

*Reference:* [arxiv/2208.14736](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14736)
**The Zariski Cancellation Problem and related problems in Affine Algebraic Geometry**
by *Neena Gupta*
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Arxiv.«2208.14736»

open Polynomial

/--
A finitely generated `k`-algebra `A` is cancellative if for all finitely generated `k` algebras `B` such that
`B[X] ≅ₖ A[X]` we have `B ≅ₖ A`.
-/
def IsCancellative (k A : Type*) [Field k]
    [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] : Prop := ∀ {B : Type*}
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra.FiniteType k B], Nonempty (A[X] ≃ₐ[k] B[X]) →
    Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[k] B)

/--
The **Zariski Cancellation Problem**: every polynomial ring over a field `k` of characteristic
`0` is cancellative.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem {k : Type*} [Field k]
    [CharZero k] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] : IsCancellative k (MvPolynomial ι k) := by
  sorry

/--
The single variable polynomial ring `k[X]` is cancellative in any characteristic
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem.variants.dim_one
    {k : Type*} [Field k] : IsCancellative k k[X] := by
  sorry

/--
The two variable polynomial ring `k[X]` is cancellative in any characteristic
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem.variants.dim_two {k : Type*} [Field k] :
    IsCancellative k (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) := by
  sorry

/--
The positive characteristic case of the Zariski Cancellation Problem is false in dimension `3`
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem.variants.false_pos_card
    (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (hι : Fintype.card ι = 3) :
    ¬ IsCancellative (ZMod p) (MvPolynomial ι (ZMod p)) := by
  sorry

end Arxiv.«2208.14736»

findings.description: The docstring calls `k[X]` a two-variable polynomial ring. In this file, `k[X]` denotes the univariate ring `Polynomial k`. The theorem itself correctly uses `MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k`, so its mathematics is intact.
findings.source_evidence: Gupta, arXiv:2208.14736, §2, the paragraph discussing Question 1′ for n=2, explicitly identifies the ring as k[X,Y] and explains that the perfect-field hypothesis can be dropped. https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14736
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to: “The two-variable polynomial ring $k[X,Y]$ is cancellative over any field $k$.” No theorem change is needed.

reformulations.difference: The source quantifies over arbitrary k-algebras B, whereas Lean additionally assumes `Algebra.FiniteType k B`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This assumption follows from the isomorphism premise. Since A is finitely generated over k, so is A[X]; an isomorphism transfers finite generation to B[X], and evaluation at X=0 exhibits B as a quotient of B[X]. Thus restricting the quantifier to finitely generated B does not change cancellativity. The equivalence is proved as `cancellation_iff_unrestricted` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: For the characteristic-zero part of Question 1′, Lean uses arbitrary finite variable-index types, including the empty type, instead of positive integers n. It also writes the polynomial-ring isomorphism through `IsCancellative`, rather than directly as B[X] ≅ₖ k[X₁,…,Xₙ₊₁].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Renaming variables identifies an index type ι with Fin(card ι), and `MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv` identifies k[X₁,…,Xₙ₊₁] with k[X₁,…,Xₙ][X]. Isomorphisms can be reversed. The additional n=0 case is true: k[X] ≅ B[X] implies B is a domain and B[X] is a principal ideal ring, hence B is a field. Evaluation at zero then supplies a k-algebra map B→k, which is injective because B is a field and surjective because it fixes k. Hence B≅ₖk. The complete equivalence, including this boundary case, is proved as `main_formulation_iff_source` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked all five declarations. No substantive mathematical misformalization was found, and all four research-status tags agree with the consulted sources. The positive-characteristic variant states the valid prime-field special case of Gupta’s stronger arbitrary-field theorem; prime-field counterexamples suffice to demonstrate the stated failure of cancellation. The hypotheses exclude ZMod 0 and ZMod 1, and the smallest permitted case p=2 is covered by Gupta’s construction. Scratch equivalence and boundary proofs compile and do not depend on sorryAx or the file’s conjectural theorems.
